integrated_report.patient_specimen_id: Case case_aml: bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy (left posterior iliac crest) from a 58-year-old man, studied by morphology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics/FISH and a myeloid NGS panel.

component_studies.accession: MMD-26-NGS-22150 (as referenced in the cytogenetics report)

integrated_report.clinical_context: 58-year-old man with 41% circulating peripheral blood blasts, undergoing bone marrow evaluation (aspirate and core biopsy, left posterior iliac crest) for suspected acute leukemia.
integrated_report.morphology_summary: The marrow is markedly hypercellular (approximately 90-95%) with extensive replacement by sheets of immature mononuclear cells and extensive blast-equivalent infiltration on the core. The 500-cell aspirate differential gives 18% blasts, with promonocytes (4%) enumerated separately. Blasts are medium-to-large with fine chromatin and one to three nucleoli; a subset has folded or indented nuclei with grayish cytoplasm and occasional fine azurophilic granulation; no definite Auer rods are seen. Erythropoiesis is left-shifted with mild megaloblastoid change, megakaryocytes are reduced, reticulin is MF-1, and storage iron is present without ring sideroblasts. Cytochemistry shows MPO positivity in a minor subset of blasts (approximately 5-10%) and NSE positivity with partial fluoride inhibition, read as a myeloid process with probable monocytic differentiation. The report notes that the blast count is likely depressed by hemodilution and by the subjectivity of promonocyte assignment, and deferred lineage confirmation and classification to flow, cytogenetic and molecular studies.
integrated_report.flow_or_ihc_summary: Eight-color flow cytometry (CD45/SSC gating; viability 94% by 7-AAD) identifies abnormal myeloid blasts at approximately 22% of total nucleated cells, expressing CD34 (subset, ~60%), CD117, bright HLA-DR, CD13, bright CD33, CD38, CD64, dim CD4 and dim cytoplasmic MPO, and negative for CD14, CD2, CD19 and cyCD3. A markedly expanded, left-shifted monocytic compartment (maturing monocytes 19% plus promonocytes/immature monocytic cells 11%, approximately 30% of TNC) shows bright uniform CD64, CD14 on the maturing fraction, CD11b, CD11c, CD36, HLA-DR and dim CD4, establishing monocytic lineage. Aberrant CD56 (partial) and CD7 (subset) are expressed on the blasts and may be used for measurable residual disease tracking. The assay is a laboratory-developed test.
integrated_report.cytogenetics_summary: G-banded karyotype (24- and 48-hour synchronized cultures, 400-425 bphs): 46,XY[20], with no clonal numerical or structural abnormality at the stated band resolution. Interphase AML FISH panel (200 nuclei per probe) is negative for RUNX1-RUNX1T1, CBFB rearrangement, PML-RARA, KMT2A rearrangement, MECOM rearrangement, -5/5q- (EGR1), -7/7q- (D7S486) and TP53 (17p13.1) deletion, all within normal cutoffs. The case is cytogenetically normal.
integrated_report.molecular_summary: Hybrid-capture 54-gene myeloid NGS panel is positive for: NPM1 type A frameshift insertion NM_002520.7:c.860_863dup p.(Trp288CysfsTer12), VAF 39%, Tier I (classifying); FLT3 internal tandem duplication, exon 14 (~36 bp), VAF 31%, ITD/WT allelic ratio 0.62, Tier I (prognostic/predictive, not classifying); and DNMT3A NM_022552.5:c.2645G>A p.(Arg882His), VAF 44%, Tier II (prognostic, not classifying). No reportable variant was detected in the listed selected genes including CEBPA, RUNX1, TP53, ASXL1, IDH1 and IDH2.
integrated_interpretation: The integrated findings establish acute myeloid leukemia: morphology, flow cytometry and the molecular report each support AML in a markedly hypercellular (approximately 90-95%) marrow extensively replaced by immature mononuclear cells, with 41% circulating peripheral blood blasts.

Myeloid lineage of the blasts is supported by cytochemical MPO positivity in a minor subset (approximately 5-10%) and by flow cytometric dim cytoplasmic MPO with CD13, CD33 and CD117, with no lymphoid lineage markers (CD2, CD19, cyCD3) expressed.

The marrow blast percentage is discordant between the 500-cell aspirate differential (18%, with promonocytes 4% counted separately) and flow cytometry (approximately 22% of total nucleated cells by CD45/side-scatter gating).

This discordance does not affect classification, because under the WHO Instructions AML with NPM1 mutation is defined by the genetic abnormality regardless of the morphologic blast count, so the historical 20% threshold does not apply.

The true blast-equivalent burden is probably at or above 20%: counting the 4% promonocytes as blast equivalents gives 22%, matching flow, the core shows extensive blast-equivalent infiltration, and the aspirate count is likely lowered by hemodilution and by subjective promonocyte assignment.

Morphology regarded monocytic differentiation as probable only (folded or indented nuclei, NSE positivity with partial fluoride inhibition), whereas flow cytometry states that the immunophenotype establishes the monocytic lineage.

This discordance is resolved as confirmed monocytic differentiation, because multiparameter immunophenotyping (bright uniform CD64, CD14 on maturing cells, CD11b, CD11c, CD36 and dim CD4 in an expanded monocytic compartment of about 30% of TNC) assigns lineage more objectively than smear morphology, and the morphology report itself deferred to flow for confirmation.
Cytogenetics reports a normal male karyotype, 46,XY[20], with a negative AML FISH panel, whereas the NGS panel is positive for an NPM1 type A frameshift, FLT3-ITD and DNMT3A R882H.

This is only an apparent conflict: these are small sequence-level variants that karyotyping and FISH cannot detect, as the cytogenetics report itself acknowledges in stating that a normal karyotype does not exclude a submicroscopic abnormality, so the case is cytogenetically normal AML with mutated NPM1.

The NPM1 type A frameshift insertion (c.860_863dup, VAF 39%, Tier I) was detectable only on the molecular (NGS) study and was invisible to morphology, flow cytometry and cytogenetics; it is the finding that assigns the case to AML with NPM1 mutation and makes the 18% versus 22% blast-threshold question irrelevant to classification.

FLT3-ITD (exon 14, about 36 bp, VAF 31%, ITD/WT allelic ratio 0.62, Tier I) was likewise detected only by NGS and was invisible to the other three studies; it does not change the disease category but is prognostically adverse and makes the patient a candidate for FLT3 inhibitor therapy.

DNMT3A R882H (VAF 44%, Tier II) was also detected only by NGS and was invisible to the other three studies; it does not define or change the WHO/ICC category and is reported as a likely clonal hematopoiesis founder event with possible prognostic relevance.

The normal karyotype and negative FISH panel (RUNX1-RUNX1T1, CBFB, PML-RARA, KMT2A, MECOM, -5/5q-, -7/7q- and TP53 deletion) were established only by cytogenetics and exclude the competing recurrent-rearrangement and cytogenetic-risk categories of AML, leaving NPM1 as the single classifying abnormality.

Aberrant CD56 (partial) and CD7 (subset) expression on the blasts was detected only by flow cytometry and was invisible to the other studies; it does not change the diagnosis but provides a leukemia-associated immunophenotype for measurable residual disease tracking.
No TP53 abnormality was identified, with FISH negative for a 17p13.1 deletion and NGS detecting no reportable TP53 variant.

Under the WHO Instructions, FLT3-ITD and DNMT3A are prognostic rather than classifying mutations, so the entity is named by the NPM1 mutation alone and not by differentiation under the AML-NOS scheme.
final_integrated_diagnosis: Bone marrow, left posterior iliac crest, aspirate and core biopsy: Acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1 mutation (WHO 5e), with monocytic differentiation.
Cytogenetically normal karyotype (46,XY[20]) with a negative AML FISH panel.

Marrow blasts 18% by manual aspirate differential (22% when the 4% promonocytes are counted as blast equivalents) and approximately 22% by flow cytometry; the 20% blast threshold does not apply to this genetically defined entity.
integrated_report.prognostic_predictive_notes: FLT3-ITD (exon 14, ~36 bp, VAF 31%, ITD/WT allelic ratio 0.62, Tier I) is reported as prognostically adverse and as a target for FLT3 inhibitor therapy; the allelic ratio is provided to support treatment decisions. DNMT3A R882H (VAF 44%, Tier II) is commonly co-mutated with NPM1 and FLT3-ITD, is frequently a clonal hematopoiesis founder event, and is reported for completeness and potential prognostic relevance; per the WHO Instructions, the co-occurrence of DNMT3A with NPM1 and FLT3-ITD is prognostically relevant. Neither FLT3-ITD nor DNMT3A defines or changes the disease category. No TP53 abnormality was detected by FISH or NGS. Aberrant CD56 (partial) and CD7 (subset) on blasts provide a leukemia-associated immunophenotype for measurable residual disease monitoring.
integrated_report.limitations_pending: Morphology: the 18% aspirate blast count is likely affected by hemodilution, promonocyte assignment on smears is subjective, and no definite Auer rods were identified. Flow cytometry: the assay is a laboratory-developed test, and the gated blast estimate (22%) is expected to differ from the manual count. Cytogenetics: results apply only at the stated band resolution (400-425 bphs) with 20 cells counted and 5 fully karyotyped, and a normal karyotype does not exclude a submicroscopic abnormality. Molecular: negative results are stated for the listed selected genes (including CEBPA, RUNX1, TP53, ASXL1, IDH1 and IDH2); the complete 54-gene list was not provided in the synthesis. Component laboratory names, most accession numbers and report dates were not provided to the integrator.
